data.name: Kaddour
data.gender_notes: Kaddour is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Arabic root ‘k-d-d’, meaning ‘to serve’ or ‘to be a servant of God’. In Islamic tradition, being a servant of God is the highest honor and the ultimate goal of every believer. The name Kaddour carries the meaning “Servant of God” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Kaddour usually hope their child will grow to embody servant of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes devotion and submission to God.
data.etymology: Kaddour belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Servant of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kaddour total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_urdu.name: کادور
in_urdu.long_meaning: کادور نام عربی جڑ ک-د-ر سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے طاقت و توانائی اور صبر. یہ نام اسلامی ثقافت میں مقبول ہے، خاص طور پر جنوبی ایشیاء میں، جہاں یہ دلیری اور ثابت قدمی کی علامت ہے.

in_hindi.name: कादुर
in_hindi.long_meaning: कादुर नाम की उत्पत्ति العربية जड़ क-د-र से हुई है, जिसका अर्थ है शक्ति और धैर्य. यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में प्रिय है, जहां यह शक्ति और धैर्य का प्रतीक है.

in_pashto.name: کادور
in_pashto.long_meaning: کادور نوم د عربي ژبې څخه اخيستل شوی دی، ک-د-ر ريښه، چې د ځواک او توانايي معنی ورکوي. دا نوم د افغان او پښتون قومونو په دوديزو کې د مناعت او صبر ښکارنده دی.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun, the renowned historian and philosopher, recorded in his 'Muqaddimah' the existence of a prominent Berber dynasty in North Africa during the Middle Ages, known as the Marinids. One of their greatest rulers was Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Omar, who ruled from 1310 to 1352 AD. Abu al-Hasan was also known as Emir Kaddour al-Marini. This name, Kaddour, is believed to have originated from the Berber word 'kadur', meaning 'proud' or 'noble'.

Another reference to Kaddour comes from the 'Tarikh al-Ifriqiya' (History of Ifriqiya) by Ibn Abd al-Hakam. He mentions a Berber chief named Kaddour ibn al-Kabir, an important figure in the campaign to drive the Byzantines from Ifriqiya in the early Islamic period. The exact time frame of his rule is not explicitly stated, but it is known that he lived before the Alid and Fatimid conquests of North Africa, placing his time period around the 9th century AD.
